title: R7: Publish rubric-dataset simulation results with caveats
description:
## Purpose

Publish the rubric-dataset simulation results.

## Content

Gap recovered over rounds per arm; explanations needed; shuffled and noisy controls; F ceiling and human ceiling; UNEXPLAINABLE rate; spend.

## Caveats (must appear)

- The stakeholder is SIMULATED: an LLM holding the guideline is a tidy compressor of it. Supports "a rubric written for humans can be transmitted as a few explanations tied to errors"; does NOT show real stakeholders explain this well, consistently or cheaply.
- Dataset-specific: license limits, contamination risk (publication year), subsetting if any, human-ceiling noise.
- One seed; development phase, exploratory.

## Definition of done

Addendum in `studies/UNIFIED_FLYWHEEL_RESULTS.md` (or a sibling results doc); decision recorded on whether to pilot the explanation channel with real reviewers; issues closed with evidence.

## Cost

$0.

comments.author: home
comments.text: FOMC was run. Results: studies/FOMC_RUBRIC_RESULTS.md. The flywheel with simulated explanations (A-c) recovered ~92% of a small 2.8-point gap (S 0.656 -> 0.682 vs labels-only/shuffled ~40-47%); the full published rubric ceiling was only 0.684. The HateCheck/SwDA held-out re-screen failed (studies/rubric_screen/screen_results.json), so no further rubric dataset is run here. Follow-up filed: epic decision-flywheel-evaluations-4a326be6-af63-44fa-b6ec-39e296713109 (streaming SME simulation on Amazon review moderation). Published in studies/FOMC_RUBRIC_RESULTS.md with caveats; definition of done met; closing.
